import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a custom order for customer age groups for better visualization and legend consistency
age_group_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']
df['customer_age_group'] = pd.Categorical(df['customer_age_group'], categories=age_group_order, ordered=True)

# Aggregate total revenue by product and customer age group
revenue_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Sort products by their total revenue in descending order for better readability
product_total_revenue = revenue_by_product_age.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False)
revenue_by_product_age = revenue_by_product_age.loc[product_total_revenue.index]

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8)) # Slightly larger figure for better detail

# Create a stacked bar chart
# Using a vibrant colormap to distinguish age groups
revenue_by_product_age.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=plt.gca(), cmap='tab20')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Total Revenue by Product, Segmented by Customer Age Group', fontsize=18, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Revenue ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend outside the plot area
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Improve layout and add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust layout to make space for the legend

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
